title: Check room, staff and finances of the Keyhole
summary: The club had a check room and kitchen, ten waitresses and a $190,000 take in nine months against a large payroll.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you have a check room there?
Sure had a massive check room. Also a kitchen. D dear to find this food, short ours.
Did you make any money out of the check room?

They had plenty of money out of the check room. Mm-hm. It wasn't real profiting. D dear to inside business, dear to dear to dear to dear to dear to dear dear dear dear You didn't even have to hire a check of the waitresses to check the property for the customer and give them those checks. They would give them a certain percentage or whatever. But I would have collected so that was another enticement for them to do a good job as a waitress. Or wait.
How many waitresses did you have?

One time I had a spirit club, I had 10 waitresses, a head waiter, and 2 car parkers on the outside of the park. This was a massive operation. It took in $190,000 the first pair of 9 months out there. But so overall, the payroll was run, as I told you yesterday, from $2,000 to $2,500. And then of course we had the taxes each quarter of the payroll. This would go up to the thousands. The profit wasn't $190,000, but a big portion of it was. You'd pay off your investment and then you'd carry the oldest of the world. The tides of South Africa.
